items.claim: Every Masoretic fact this row asserts is true on the witness. A petuchah is recorded after MT 37:14, and that verse genuinely stacks three refrain-grade closes: the second-person-plural recognition variant (a 21-verse family), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (14 verses) and the short utterance signature carrying no divine-name pair (4 verses: MT 13:6, 13:7, 16:58, 37:14). items.claim: Two Masoretic statements in this row are false on the witness. (1) A setumah IS recorded on MT 37:28, which is the span's own final verse, so the row's denial that no setumah or petuchah falls anywhere inside MT 37:15-28 is untrue as written; what the witness supports is the narrower fact that MT 37:16 through MT 37:27 carry no parashah mark at all, which is what the two candidate interior cuts the row is rejecting actually need. The row elsewhere cites that same MT 37:28 mark as its own close, so the denial also contradicts the row's own rationale. (2) MT 37:16 carries two read-form notes, and the row presents them as the same read form; in the witness the second note's read form differs from the first in its accent, carrying U+05BD METEG where the first carries U+0591 ETNAHTA. A single read form stated for both notes therefore misdescribes the witness at MT 37:16.

items.claim: The row asserts a recognition close at MT 39:23, and the witness does not support it. The corpus defines the wide recognition family as a verse in which the knowing clause and 'that I am YHWH' stand together, so MT 39:23 is not a member of it and is not refrain-grade close evidence. The nations-addressed recognition verses of this chapter are MT 39:6 and MT 39:7, both outside this row's span. The row's companion claim at MT 39:22 is correct: that verse does carry the wide-family expansion in which the house of Israel knows, and it is not in the strict 28.

Removing the false MT 39:23 claim weakens neither side, because the row already treats MT 39:22 and MT 39:23 as paragraph-internal rather than row-final; what changes is that only one wide-family recognition verse, MT 39:22, actually stands inside the span.

e19_selfreport: I ran no listing, no glob, no recursive search and no existence check against any directory, my own scratch included.
